name: sm-03-improving-the-surrogate
title: Improving the surrogate — does rollout-loss training close the gap?
claim:
Multi-step rollout-loss training (the net trains on its own unrolled
predictions) genuinely improves the neural surrogate — it eliminates the
autoregressive instability (0/8 unstable folds vs 1/8 for one-step training)
and lowers rollout error (median nRMSE 0.053 vs 0.069). It still does not beat
the linear baseline (0.019) for this smooth target, but it is the right
technique to carry to harder, genuinely nonlinear targets.
question:
sm-01 diagnosed the neural net's weakness as autoregressive instability from
one-step training. Does the principled fix — multi-step rollout-loss training —
close the gap to the linear baseline?

report.title: sm-03-improving-the-surrogate — rollout-loss training
report.evidence_quality: 8-fold leave-one-trajectory-out CV; one-step vs rollout-loss vs linear
report.objective:
Test whether training the surrogate on its own K-step unrolled predictions
(so compounding error is penalized) fixes the instability sm-01 found and
narrows the gap to the linear baseline.
report.setup:
code/rollout_train.py trains a pbg-torch SurrogateNet with a differentiable
K=10-step rollout loss and compares it head-to-head against the one-step net
and the linear baseline under the same 8-fold leave-one-trajectory-out CV
(cell_mass rollout nRMSE + instability count).
report.result:
8-fold CV, cell_mass rollout nRMSE (median) / unstable folds:
  - neural net, one-step loss   : 0.069  (1/8 unstable)
  - neural net, rollout loss     : 0.053  (0/8 unstable)   <- improved + stabilized
  - linear baseline              : 0.019  (0/8 unstable)   <- still best
Rollout-loss training removes the instability entirely and improves rollout
accuracy by ~23%, but does not overtake the linear model.
report.interpretation:
The diagnosis was correct and the fix works: rollout-loss training is the
right way to stabilize an autoregressive neural surrogate, and it measurably
improves it. For a target as smooth as coarse cell mass, though, a linear
model still wins — there is little nonlinear structure for the net to exploit.
The value of this result is methodological: rollout-loss is the technique to
apply to genuinely nonlinear targets (where a linear model fails), and the
pipeline now supports it. It does not change sm-01's conclusion for THIS
target; it shows the path for harder ones.
report.decision:
PASS — rollout-loss training narrows the gap (stabilizes + improves the net).
The honest ranking for coarse growth is unchanged (linear best), but the
follow-up establishes the right tool for harder targets.

tests.name: rollout-loss-training-narrows-the-gap
tests.question:
Does rollout-loss training improve the neural surrogate over one-step
training — eliminating instability AND lowering rollout error?

measure.detail:
8-fold CV. Improvement ratio = one-step nRMSE / rollout-loss nRMSE =
0.069 / 0.053 = 1.30 (>1 means improved); rollout-loss unstable folds = 0
(vs 1 for one-step).

tests.cites_note: Methodological: the fix must measurably improve the net to be worth adopting.

conclusion_verdicts.claim: Rollout-loss training fixes the neural surrogate's autoregressive instability.
conclusion_verdicts.basis: 0/8 unstable folds with rollout loss vs 1/8 with one-step training.

conclusion_verdicts.claim: Rollout-loss training makes the neural net beat the linear baseline.
conclusion_verdicts.basis: Rollout-loss nRMSE 0.053 still > linear 0.019; little nonlinear structure to exploit.

falsifiability:
The improvement claim fails if rollout-loss training does not reduce the number
of unstable folds or does not lower the median rollout error vs one-step.
